scope.top_bubble: Classical mechanics fundamentals through Lagrangian formulation

nodes.title: Lagrangian Mechanics
nodes.one_liner: Reformulation of classical mechanics using the principle of least action
outcomes: Derive equations of motion from a Lagrangian
Apply the Euler-Lagrange equation to simple systems
Identify when Lagrangian methods simplify a problem

nodes.title: Euler-Lagrange Equation
nodes.one_liner: The fundamental equation of the calculus of variations applied to mechanics
outcomes: Derive the Euler-Lagrange equation from Hamilton's principle
Apply it to find equations of motion

nodes.title: Generalized Coordinates
nodes.one_liner: Choosing coordinates that respect the constraints of a mechanical system
outcomes: Express kinetic and potential energy in generalized coordinates

nodes.title: Calculus of Variations
outcomes: Derive the Euler-Lagrange equation for a general functional

nodes.title: Newton's Laws of Motion
nodes.one_liner: The three foundational laws governing force and motion
outcomes: State and apply Newton's three laws

nodes.title: Energy Conservation
nodes.one_liner: Work-energy theorem and conservation of mechanical energy
outcomes: Apply conservation of energy to mechanical systems

nodes.title: Partial Derivatives
nodes.one_liner: Differentiation of functions of several variables with respect to one variable
outcomes: Apply the chain rule for multivariable functions

nodes.title: Integration Techniques
nodes.one_liner: Methods for evaluating integrals beyond basic antiderivatives

nodes.title: Vectors and Coordinate Systems
nodes.one_liner: Vector algebra and non-Cartesian coordinate systems
outcomes: Express physical quantities in polar/spherical coordinates

nodes.title: Work and Kinetic Energy
nodes.one_liner: The relationship between force, displacement, and energy transfer
outcomes: Calculate work done by a force

nodes.title: Constraints and Degrees of Freedom
nodes.one_liner: How constraints reduce the configuration space of a mechanical system

nodes.title: D'Alembert's Principle
nodes.one_liner: Virtual work principle bridging Newton's laws and analytical mechanics
outcomes: Derive equations of motion using virtual work

edges.justification: Euler-Lagrange equation is the core computational tool of Lagrangian mechanics
Lagrangian is expressed in generalized coordinates; cannot formulate without them
D'Alembert's principle motivates the Lagrangian formulation from Newton's laws
Euler-Lagrange equation IS the calculus of variations applied to the action functional
The equation involves partial derivatives of the Lagrangian with respect to q and q-dot
Generalized coordinates are chosen to automatically satisfy constraints
Coordinate transformations are the mechanical skill underlying generalized coordinates
Functionals are defined as integrals; evaluating them requires integration techniques
Deriving the Euler-Lagrange equation from a functional requires partial differentiation
D'Alembert's principle reformulates Newton's second law using virtual displacements
Virtual work is defined relative to constraint surfaces
Virtual work is the conceptual bridge; requires understanding work as force times displacement
Constraints are expressed as equations relating coordinate variables
Energy conservation is derived from the work-energy theorem

_test_notes.description: 12-node fixture for unlock-computation unit tests. Statuses pre-set to exercise all four UnlockStatus values. The unlock rule: completed/in_progress pass through from node.status; not_started nodes are 'unlocked' iff ALL children have status=completed, else 'locked'. Leaf nodes (no children) with status=not_started are 'unlocked'.
